study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual deviations from normative models of brain structure in a large cross-sectional schizophrenia cohort

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Objectives are explicitly stated: to map individual deviations from normative ranges of brain structure and to evaluate whether these individual loci align with group-average maps; additionally, to explore genetic/clinical drivers. The purpose of normative modeling (to parse heterogeneity and guide personalized interventions) is also described. Both required criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We aimed to map deviations from normative ranges of brain structure for individual patients and evaluate whether the loci of individual deviations recapitulated group-average brain maps of schizophrenia pathology. … We conclude that anatomical loci of schizophrenia-related changes are highly heterogeneous … Normative modeling can aid in parsing schizophrenia heterogeneity and guiding personalized interventions.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model. It clearly describes eligibility criteria for healthy controls (ASRB dataset), exclusion criteria (neurological disorder, head trauma with amnesia >24h, IQ<70, substance dependence, recent ECT), image quality standards (exclude MRI artifacts, motion, cropping), and reports final sample sizes with exclusion notes. All listed criteria for NEW models are satisfied.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Participants comprising the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank [28] … were considered eligible. After excluding participants due to MRI artifacts, a total of 517 individuals remained … 322 … schizophrenia … and 195 … healthy comparison individuals. … Exclusion criteria included any neurological disorder, history of brain trauma … intellectual disability (full-scale IQ < 70), current drug or alcohol dependence, as well as electroconvulsive therapy in the past 6 months. … Participants showing gross artifacts, cerebellar cropping and/or significant head motion were excluded…

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates age and sex are modeled explicitly in the quantile regression formulation. Multi-site data are addressed by harmonization procedures and by including acquisition site as a nuisance confound in the model.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Quantile regression … enabled … percentiles expressed as a function of age and sex. … For the healthy participant with index i … C_i encapsulates nuisance confounds, including acquisition site. … the diffusion-weighted images were retrospectively harmonized to alleviate possible nonlinear site-related differences.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Data source for the reference cohort is specified: healthy adults from the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB), with citation to the original publication.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Here, we developed normative models … using harmonized MRI data from healthy adults … participating in the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank [28]. … Participants … were recruited from five sites in Australia … as described in detail elsewhere [28].

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Primary data acquisition details are provided: modality subtypes (T1-weighted structural MRI and diffusion-weighted MRI), acquisition parameters (TR, TE, resolution, b-value, directions), and equipment specifications (Siemens Avanto; five scanner sites). All required elements for PRIMARY data are present.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Structural and diffusion-weighted MRI … were acquired using Siemens Avanto MRI scanners … The same acquisition sequence was used at all sites. Structural T1-weighted … MPRAGE (voxel resolution: 1 mm^3 isotropic, TR: 1980 ms, TE: 4.3 ms). Diffusion-weighted images … 64 non-collinear gradient directions … (b value: 1000 s/mm^2, voxel resolution: 2.4 mm^3 isotropic, TR: 8400 ms, TE: 88 ms).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are described: FSL 5.11 (eddy correction, tensor fitting), ANTs normalization, atlas averaging for FA; FreeSurfer 6.0 with standard recon steps for cortical thickness; QC exclusions stated. All relevant criteria are satisfied.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: Fractional anisotropy (FA) images were computed … using FSL 5.11 … Eddy … distortions and head motion … corrected using the eddy tool in FSL. … FA images were normalized … using the ANTs package … averaged … ICBM-DTI-81 white matter atlas. … Structural images were processed using Freesurfer 6.0 … Preprocessing included motion correction, intensity normalization, non-brain tissue removal … The reconstructed surfaces were not manually edited.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For the NEW model, the study uses explicit internal validation via repeated random splits under a tenfold cross-validation framework (train n=175; test n=20) and assesses coverage of the normative range on held-out healthy individuals.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Percentile curves were fitted using a randomly selected subset of healthy individuals (n = 175, training set) … remaining healthy individuals … (n = 20, test set). This was repeated … using a tenfold cross-validation framework. … more than 90% of the healthy individuals in each test set resided within the normative range.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The NEW normative model was developed and validated within the ASRB dataset; there is no application to an independent external healthy dataset. All participants were drawn from ASRB across five Australian sites.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Participants comprising the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank [28] … Participants were recruited from five sites in Australia …

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is specified as quantile regression; key settings include modeling percentiles as functions of age, sex, and nuisance confounds (including site), bootstrapped confidence intervals, and inclusion of age-squared where needed. Software is specified as MATLAB quantreg with code availability.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: Quantile regression … was used to determine percentile curves … expressed as a function of age and sex. … C_i encapsulates nuisance confounds, including acquisition site. … Shading indicates 95% confidence intervals, estimated with bootstrapping (n = 1000). … The Matlab function quantreg was used … This code is publicly accessible.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is assessed quantitatively by coverage: in cross-validated test sets, >90% of healthy individuals fall within the 5–95% normative range for all regions/tracts. This directly evaluates calibration of the percentile estimates.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: >90% of the healthy individuals in each test set resided within the normative range (5–95% percentiles).

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: … 322 … individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder … Exclusion criteria included any neurological disorder … intellectual disability (full-scale IQ < 70), current drug or alcohol dependence, as well as electroconvulsive therapy in the past 6 months. … Participants showing gross artifacts, cerebellar cropping and/or significant head motion were excluded …

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: Individuals with schizophrenia completed assessments … Independent component analysis was used to parse 82 of the assessment scales into four latent dimensions … CCA … identified a marginally significant mode of association between the four dimensions and the deviation scores …

Clinical implications are discussed via associations with symptom dimensions and polygenic risk, and the broader interpretation about heterogeneity and potential for personalized interventions is articulated.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: … individuals were classified as either within the normative range … (5–95% percentiles), infra-normal (<5% percentile) or supra-normal (>95% percentile). … CCA … identified a … association between the four dimensions and the deviation scores … Higher polygenic risk for schizophrenia associated with a greater number of regions with infra-normal deviations in CT … Normative modeling can aid in parsing schizophrenia heterogeneity and guiding personalized interventions.
